pairs.question: Roscio cur tanti fuerint causam requiro. Egebat?
pairs.derivation: Authorial Q&A. Kept the prior sentence 'Roscio cur tanti fuerint causam requiro' as verbatim setup so that the subject of 'Egebat?' (Roscius) has a referent. Answer is the immediately following retort, complete to its full stop; stopped before the next question 'Debebat?'.

pairs.question: Debebat?
pairs.derivation: Authorial Q&A within the same run about Roscius's wealth. Subject Roscius is established by the surrounding context. Answer is the contiguous reply, complete to its full stop; stopped before 'Avarus erat?'.

pairs.question: Avarus erat?
pairs.answer: Immo etiam ante quam locuples esset, semper liberalissimus munificentissimusque fuit.
pairs.derivation: Authorial Q&A continuing the run about Roscius's character. Stripped the editorial angle brackets in '<esset>' keeping the word 'esset'. Answer is the full contiguous reply to its terminal full stop; the section marker [23] follows.

pairs.question: Panurgum tu, Saturi, proprium Fanni dicis fuisse. At ego totum Rosci fuisse contendo. Quid erat enim Fanni?
pairs.derivation: Authorial Q&A. Kept the two prior verbatim sentences as setup so that 'Quid erat enim Fanni?' has its referent (Panurgus the slave's value, Fannius's vs Roscius's share). Answer is the one-word reply; stopped before the next question 'Quid Rosci?'.

pairs.question: Quid Rosci?
pairs.derivation: Authorial Q&A immediately following, contrasting Roscius's share of Panurgus. Answer is the one-word reply, complete; 'Facies non erat...' follows as elaboration.

pairs.question: Quis iudex? Cluvius. Quid is dicit?
pairs.answer: HS ccciccc Panurgi nomine Flavium Fannio dissolvisse.
pairs.derivation: Authorial Q&A. Kept 'Quis iudex? Cluvius.' as verbatim setup so 'is' in 'Quid is dicit?' has its referent (the iudex Cluvius). Answer is the contiguous reported reply to its full stop; the following 'Quem tu si ex censu spectas...' is elaboration and was cut.
